title: Enterprise signal synthesis and prioritization for hosted chat/streaming/tool-request intake
creator: Lucia Park
description:
Summary: We need a single, explainable intake scoring function and routing rules for Hosted API feature requests that blends enterprise signals (SLA needs, compliance/regulatory constraints, ARR/tier, and legal retention requirements) with product/technical signals (streaming/tool-calls complexity, structured output requirements, expected QPS and latency sensitivity). Goal is to reduce manual Triage time by 40% and surface a prioritized queue that maps cleanly to Sales/CS SLAs, Eng scheduling, and Console roadmap lanes.

Scope:
- Inputs: customer-submitted form + support tickets + CSM/AE intake notes + sales contracts (metadata) + usage telemetry when available.
- Outputs: (1) priority score (0-100) with breakdown by signal, (2) routing action: auto-backlog / fast-track review / require architecture & security review / sales escalation, (3) recommended initial owner (PM, Solutions Eng, Eng Lead), (4) suggested SLA class (standard / elevated / enterprise-only).

Key signals and weighting (proposal):
- Customer tier / ARR / strategic (30)
- SLA / latency requirement (20)
- Regulatory / compliance flag (20)
- Feature technical risk (streaming, tool-calls, structured outputs) (15)
- Observed usage or PoC traction (10)
- Estimated implementation effort (5)
Rationale: weight toward business impact and compliance for enterprise customers while keeping technical risk visible so Eng scheduling is realistic.

Acceptance criteria:
- Triage pipeline implements score and returns explanation for each top signal (for auditability).
- Routing rules applied in 90% of test cases from historical backlog (sample of 300 requests from last 12 months).
- Dashboard in Console (triage view) shows top 5 pending requests with signal breakdown and responsible owner.
- Integration points built: CSM intake form -> triage service, hooks to Sales contract metadata, and link-out to Confluence requirement doc.

Trade-offs and design notes:
- Simpler boolean gating (e.g., any regulatory flag => immediate security review) is easy but causes many false-positives; instead we recommend a two-step pattern: soft-score then deterministic overrides for critical flags (e.g., export control) to avoid overtriage.
- Heavier weighting on ARR helps Sales/CS but risks deprioritizing lower-revenue-but-high-usage features; mitigate by exposing usage signal prominently in explanation UI.
- We will initially implement scoring in the PM service (near-term) and instrument for moving to a separate microservice if query load increases.

Engineering asks / dependencies:
- ENG: canonicalize intake payload schema (ENG-8021) and expose contract metadata from CRM.
- ENG: add new triage fields to Console API for display (ENG-9025).

Risks:
- Incorrect mappings of contract metadata could misclassify priority; plan: sample audits for first 6 weeks.
- Security review surface area may expand if we fast-track many streaming/tool requests; mitigation: cap fast-track for only customers with active enterprise contracts and explicit security accept.

Validation plan / success metrics:
- Reduce manual triage time by 40% within 8 weeks of rollout.
- 85% alignment between auto-prioritized queue and PM/Eng consensus in blind review of 100 tickets.
- Mean time to first response for high-priority enterprise requests < 48 hours.

Next steps (short-term):
- This week: finalize signal weights and deterministic override list (Owner: Ravi).
- Week 1: ENG to expose CRM contract metadata + process sample backlog (ENG-8021).
- Week 2: Ship hidden-alpha triage view and run blind alignment experiment with 50 past tickets.
- Week 3-4: Iterate weights based on feedback, expand to 300-ticket sample, roll to pilot with 3 CSMs.
